messages:
morgan: Heads-up — seeing a cluster of support tickets asking for better streaming semantics when function/tool calls are invoked mid-answer. Ticket examples: https://zendesk.company/agent/tickets/8921 and 8956. Customers want: 1) interleaved tool-call progress events, 2) deterministic end-of-call markers, and 3) structured partial outputs for downstream processing.
neeraj: Thanks Morgan. Are these enterprise customers or self-serve? any SLA implications? :eyes:
morgan: Mix — 8921 is enterprise (Dedicated), 8956 is self-serve but high volume. Both hit issues when tool runtimes exceed 5s and the client gives up.
emily: Can you paste a minimal repro (payload + client behavior) so we can see where the stream is dropping?
morgan: Pasted minimal repro inline:```curl -N -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream 
-H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
-d '{"model":"rwd-3b", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Run image-gen and return metadata"}], "functions":[{"name":"image-gen","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"url":{"type":"string"}}}}]}'```
Client observes: stream emits partial tokens, then a JSON function call start event, then no more events for ~10s and client times out. When tool finishes, a final function call completion event arrives but no structured partial outputs in between.
jess: Sounds like we need streaming hooks for function_call events and an explicit chunked structured output protocol, e.g., emit events: function_call:start, function_call:chunk (with schema marker), function_call:end. That way consumers can process partial tool outputs.
neeraj: Prioritization ask: is this a breaking bug for enterprise SLAs or a feature improvement? If it's an enterprise outage risk we should fast-track.
emily: For Dedicated customers hitting SLAs it's higher priority. For self-serve, we can scope as beta feature behind a flag. Implementation effort: runtime change to propagate function-call events immediately + API contract update (semantics + examples) + SDK changes. I'd estimate 3-4 sprints (eng team of 3).
morgan: Customer asks also mentioned wanting deterministic "end-of-call" markers so clients can cleanly resume. Agree that's API-level contract.
jess: Also need to consider KV cache & batching implications — streaming a function call that triggers long token generation could block batching heuristics. We should add a fallback policy to limit blocking for other requests.
neeraj: Proposed scope for initial launch (MVP): 1) stream function_call:start and function_call:end events, 2) allow optional function_call:chunk with small JSON blobs, 3) document the new event types and update SDKs for JS/Python, 4) behind a feature flag for Hosted & Dedicated, opt-in for Private. Launch criteria: integration test for ordering guarantees, perf regression <5% p50 latency, rollout plan with canary (5% traffic) + automatic rollback if error rate spike >1%.
emily: Acceptance tests to add: -> unit tests for event ordering, -> e2e with simulated long-running tool, -> backwards compatibility test (clients not expecting new events still work).
morgan: Customer comms: need an interim workaround: recommend increasing client-side timeouts and polling the ticketing endpoint for function completion. I'll send a KB article.
jess: Engineering notes: runtime change points: event serializer, network streaming buffer, and SDK parsers. Also add metrics: function_stream_chunks, function_stream_lateness.
neeraj: OK assigning owner: emily will be PM-eng lead, jess will own runtime changes, morgan will own customer comms and support playbook. Can we add this to the product backlog with label "customer-request:streaming-tool-calls"?
morgan: Added to backlog as ticket PROD-1432 and linked the two customer tickets.
triage-bot: CREATED PROD-1432 by morgan: Customer request - streaming function_call events + structured partial outputs (priority: P2).
neeraj: Timeline proposal: spec doc + acceptance criteria this week, spike in eng for 1 sprint, implement + SDKs over next 2 sprints, beta rollout end of quarter. If Dedicated SLA customers push, we can accelerate.
emily: I'll draft the spec in product/notes and ping here when ready. Anyone object to the proposed scope?
jess: No objections. :thumbsup:
morgan: Thanks all — I'll notify the customers and link the KB. Follow-ups: emily will @ here when spec is up, jess will post initial spike findings.
neeraj: Great. Closing thread for now, will reopen if blockers appear.
